To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we present the first deep CNN designed specifically for 2D face recognition and (2) we present a method for large-scale 3D face dataset generation, training a deep CNN on this dataset and testing on the largest 3D face test dataset.

(i) we propose a method to generate a large 3D face dataset for training and a large test dataset for evaluation (ii) We propose the first deep network designed for 3D facial recognition and show its efficacy for large scale 3DFR (iii) We show that our method can be extended to the open world 3D face matching problem.

we propose the first end-to-end 3D face deep learning network and a large 3D face dataset for training and testing and demonstrate the efficacy of our approach for large-scale 3D face identification and open world face recognition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
learning from millions of 3D scans to develop a robust large-scale 3D face representation.
developing large scale 3d face recognition systems for open world face recognition and is the first of its kind.
developing a large-scale 3D face database for training, a protocol for merging existing 3D databases for testing and a CNN for large-scale 3 D face recognition.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our work is the first to report large-scale 3D face identification and verification results using deep CNNs trained on a large-scale 3d dataset.
the deep network trained on 3D face scans is the first network to surpass human performance in face recognition and is also the first deep network to be trained on 3 million facial images.
our work is the first to demonstrate large scale 3d face recognition and the first to use deep learning on 3D facial data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our network trained with our dataset outperforms state-of-the-art 3D and 2D face recognition systems by a large margin.

we are able to train a deep network on a large dataset of 3D scans of 100,000 identities and test it on a dataset of 1,853 and 31,000 identities, which is 50x larger than the previous state of the art.
we are able to achieve a recognition accuracy of 97.4% on a dataset of over 31K 3D facial probes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
3D face images can be used to train deep networks for face recognition.
deep learning can be successfully applied to 3D face data to achieve state-of-the-art performance in 3D face verification and 3D open world face recognition.
large scale 3 D face recognition is possible and it is a promising direction for future research.
